Wearing protective overgarments adds 10°F (5.6°C) to the wet bulb globe temperature index and if conducting moderate or hard work and wearing protective overgarments, add 20°F (10.2°C) to wet bulb globe temperature index. Wearing body armor increases this by another 5°F (2.8°C). A worker may produce as much as 2 to 3 gallons of sweat in the course of a day’s work. Because many heat disorders/injuries involve excessive dehydration of the body, it is essential that water intake during the workday be about equal to the amount of sweat produced. 15
